clue.text: Look towards daughter wearing right cosmetic

parts.note: to face something is to look towards it

indicators.note: something worn is put on around the wearer, so one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: a right or authority to act is a power
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone glances at their daughter, who is wearing the right make-up for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as 'correct' describing the cosmetic, but it is the noun meaning authority, which wears the daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Face powder is a make-up product dusted on the skin, so it is a type of cosmetic.

clue.text: Celebrity in Cardiff, American

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their join

parts.note: the last letter of the city's name plus the first three of the next word

explanation.surface: An American enjoys being famous in the Welsh capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity as an abstract noun means the state of being widely known, a synonym for renown.

clue.text: Dupe kind companion

parts.note: to con someone is to trick or dupe them
a kind of thing is a sort

explanation.surface: Someone fools a good-natured friend who trusted them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as the adjective 'nice' describing the companion, but it is the noun meaning type.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or partner, especially of a monarch, so a close companion.

clue.text: Experience the worst extremes, as worker in sewer might?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sink to the lowest point of misery
second meaning, taken literally: what a pipe tradesman does working deep below ground

explanation.surface: Someone who suffers terribly is compared to a man working down in the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally: a plumber working deep in a sewer is, quite literally, plumbing the depths; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reach the lowest possible level of unhappiness or bad behaviour.

clue.text: Comedian, tired after second of shows, is taken out

parts.note: a wit is a person who makes clever jokes

indicators.note: only the letter in position two of the following word is used

parts.note: the second letter of the word
a drawn face looks tired and strained

explanation.surface: An exhausted comedian is carried off after the second performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the tired word after the second letter, which follows the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or troops withdrawn have been removed or taken out of where they were.

clue.text: Girl writer deserted to run off with another?

indicators.note: the writer has left the girl's name, so those letters drop out of it

parts.note: a girl's name
a pen is a writing instrument, the usual crossword writer

explanation.surface: A girl abandoned by her author boyfriend goes off with someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove PEN from the front of PENELOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly with a lover, usually to marry.

clue.text: Not working, one on dole lacking nothing!

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is missing from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A jobless person on benefit is complaining of having no money.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLE loses its O; 'dole' is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes someone or something unemployed or inactive, out of work.

clue.text: Eccentric over at university, the French count

indicators.note: turned over, so the word before it is read from right to left

parts.note: a card is an amusing, eccentric person
U is the abbreviation for university
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: An oddball has gone back up to university to study French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a verb but names a nobleman, the vampire of Bram Stoker's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula is the vampire aristocrat of Stoker's novel, so a nobleman of that rank.

clue.text: Car or inheritance tax?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: the duty or tax payable on an estate car
the old name for the tax on a dead person's property

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tax is levied on vehicles or on what is left in a will.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a British station wagon, so a duty on one would be 'estate duty'; the real meaning is the tax on a deceased person's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate duty was the British levy on property passing at death, replaced by inheritance tax.

clue.text: Meat dish given duke following complaint

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the complaint is written first and the duke after it

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
the Duke of Wellington, victor of Waterloo

explanation.surface: A duke grumbles about the meal he has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the duke after the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef Wellington is fillet steak baked in pastry, a classic main course.

clue.text: Search for fugitive knight hiding in shed on isle

indicators.note: in an across answer, sitting on something means coming after it, so the island goes first

parts.note: the Isle of Man

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A knight on the run is hiding out in a shed on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland; 'isle' alone is the usual crossword pointer to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organised search for a person, typically an escaped criminal.

clue.text: Exaggerate about something done

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
an act is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about something that has been done.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to perform with exaggerated emotion or gesture.

clue.text: Such as dates that can't be kept?

definitions.text: Such as dates that can't be kept?

parts.words: Such as dates that can't be kept?
parts.note: surface reading: appointments that will have to be cancelled

parts.words: Such as dates that can't be kept?
parts.note: setter's reading: dates are a fruit, and these are ones you are not allowed to keep or have

explanation.walkthrough: Dates looks like diary appointments, but they are the fruit; fruit you are prohibited from having is the biblical temptation of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names something desirable that is prohibited, originally the fruit Eve was told not to eat.

clue.text: Miserly person embarrassed current collector

parts.note: to feel cheap is to feel ashamed or embarrassed
a skate is a sliding contact that picks up electric current from a conductor rail

explanation.surface: A miser is shamed over a device for gathering electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current collector' looks like someone hoarding money, but it is the electrical pick-up on a train or tram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy, mean person who avoids spending money.

clue.text: Snag affected church

parts.note: something hit badly is adversely affected
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A problem has affected the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a temporary difficulty or obstacle, the same as a snag.

clue.text: Girl fronting group wanting ribbon for hair …

indicators.note: fronting means standing at the front, so the girl comes before the group

parts.note: a girl's name
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A girl leading a pop group wants a ribbon for her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alice band, named after Tenniel's illustrations of Alice in Wonderland, is a hairband.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alice band is a broad hair band or ribbon worn across the head to hold hair back.

clue.text: In Christmas period, old eccentric may show bad taste

parts.note: taken as written
Christmas falls in December, abbreviated DEC
O is a standard abbreviation for old
rum is an old British word for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: An odd old relative behaves tactlessly over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper or unseemly behaviour, a lack of good taste.

clue.text: … left group to get one during commercial

indicators.note: happening during something means falling within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
a band is a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician walked out of the band to appear in a TV advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue only for the surface. 'group to get one' are joined first, and the pair goes inside the commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means left behind or deserted, past tense of a verb of leaving.

clue.text: A mostly forthright party delivering fruit

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
someone vocal speaks out frankly
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An outspoken group hands out fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree, often eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: I'm driven through illuminated border

indicators.note: a thing driven through another is pushed into its middle, so it sits inside

parts.note: lit means lighted up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver says they were driven through a brightly lit frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or edge, the same sense as border.

clue.text: Leather supplied by second Italian boy

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
an Italian boy's name

explanation.surface: An Italian lad provides the second consignment of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine goatskin leather, originally made in North Africa.

clue.text: Excited, gents in chopper leaving mall

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Thrilled men climb out of a helicopter at a mall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is an enclosed complex of shops, which Britons call a shopping centre.

clue.text: Lowest point in ruptured drain

indicators.note: something ruptured is burst apart, so its letters are broken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A burst drain marks the low point of someone's week.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, originally the point of the sky directly below an observer.

clue.text: Alert agent catching leader of ring

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A watchful secret agent nabs the head of a criminal ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and active, especially of an older person, so mentally alert and nimble.

clue.text: Ill at ease, a graduate approaching cast

parts.note: taken as written
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate's degree
a snake casts or sheds its skin

explanation.surface: A nervous graduate approaches the cast of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors but is the verb meaning to throw off.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means embarrassed and disconcerted, so uncomfortable in company.

clue.text: Restrict charges to be made for weaving a carpet

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into a new pattern, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fees are to be limited for making a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were British local property taxes; the government could rate-cap a council, limiting what it charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate-cap is to impose a ceiling on the local taxes a council may levy.

clue.text: Archer's painful back

indicators.note: going back means moving the opposite way, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: An archer complains of an aching back.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is'. 'back' looks like the body part but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros, Greek god of love, shoots arrows to make people fall in love, so he is a bowman.

clue.text: Bluff new blue following piece of publicity

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the colour word goes after the publicity piece

parts.note: a promo is a promotional item
N is the abbreviation for new
blue is the colour of the British Conservative Party, the Tories

explanation.surface: A newly elected Conservative is bluffing after a publicity stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' is not deceit but a steep headland. Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a high steep cliff or bank, and a promontory is a headland jutting into the sea.
